inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation p.13 ('Share Based Compensation' 1,191) and Note 18/21 share-based payment reserve movement (3,959->4,069); no separately disclosed cash tax withheld on equity-award net-share settlement (EquityAwardTaxes KPI = 0), so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc
inputs.wacc_rationale: 12.5% built on NZD/USD-blended small-cap growth software risk: IKE's cash flows are substantially USD-generated (US utility/telecom customers via ikeGPS Inc) but consolidated and reported in NZD, and the stock is a micro-cap (~NZ$220m) dual-listed on NZX/ASX with real execution risk (three unlaunched FY27 products, a still-negative owner-FCF base, and a multi-year history of dilutive raises before recent EBITDA inflection). This sits above the ~9-10.5% used for mature US SaaS/industrials and below distressed-shell levels, reflecting genuine but moderating risk now that the balance sheet is strong (net cash > 1x revenue, no debt) and monthly underlying EBITDA has turned positive.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial: lease liabilities are only NZ$0.648m at FY2026 year-end (small NZ/US office leases) against total assets and cash of NZ$32.8m; not adjusted for and not included in net debt.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component build), per dcf-methods SKILL.md routing table -- IKE is an operating vertical-SaaS/hardware-analytics company with a genuine (if currently negative) forward free-cash-flow stream, not a REIT/bank/LIC/holdco/distressed shell, so the owner-FCF engine applies directly. No prior DCF or Drivers file existed (fresh build). Presentation currency is NZD (ikeGPS Ltd functional currency NZD; ikeGPS Inc subsidiary functional currency USD, translated -- FY26 Annual Report note 2, line ~2652-2658) and the NZX/ASX quote is also NZD, so no currency-suffixed twin is required; USD/NZD translation risk is a real qualitative risk (flagged in Analysis JSON) but not a reporting-vs-quote currency split for this ticker. Net cash = cash_and_equivalents (11.700) + TermDeposits KPI (21.101) = 32.801, per financial-parser note that FY2026 core_metrics 'cash' captures only the cash-and-equivalents line. last_fcf (owner FCF) = reported_fcf (-5.325) - sbc_incl_equity_taxes (1.191) - interest_income (0.449) = -6.965; interest income stripped because net cash (32.8m) > 1x the FCF base and is added back via net_debit at the end of the DCF. Shares held flat at the FY2026 year-end fully diluted count (194.116m) -- options/other potential shares are anti-dilutive in the current loss position per Note 19, and SBC is fully expensed in the flows (share_count_basis below). No buybacks (buyback_cash 0) and no dividends -- all historical cash needs have been funded by dilutive equity raises (most recently the Aug-2025 ~NZ$27.2m institutional placement/SPP), which is exactly why the count moved 161.06m (FY2025) -> 194.12m (FY2026): that is genuine non-SBC issuance (a capital raise), not something the flat-count SBC convention should hide, so the historical per-share series is naturally discontinuous around FY2026 and the CAGR calculations below use total revenue/equity rather than per-share metrics for that reason. Cash tax rate held at 0% across all three scenarios for the full 10-year horizon: NZ accumulated losses of ~NZ$113.8m (share capital NZ$134.5m vs accumulated losses ~NZ$113.8m per Analysis JSON) plus separate US NOLs at ikeGPS Inc are large enough that even the bull case's cumulative projected EBIT (~NZ$55m over 10 years) does not exhaust the shield -- this is a calculated, not assumed, result (see cumulative-EBIT check in the build).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management-disclosed platform subscription revenue growth (FY26 actual +33% YoY; FY27 guidance 33-35%), not a blended total-revenue or equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Total-revenue and shareholders'-equity CAGRs are not usable growth proxies for this company and diverge sharply from the actual underlying growth rate. Total revenue swung from a FY2023 spike (NZ$30.8m, driven by a one-off surge in the lower-margin Platform Transactions/hardware lines) through a FY2024 trough (NZ$21.1m) back to NZ$26.5m in FY2026, giving a nonsensical -4.8% 3yr CAGR and a distorted +23.3% 5yr CAGR that partly reflects the FY2021 COVID-depressed base rather than steady compounding. Shareholders' equity CAGR is also unusable: equity has been driven almost entirely by the timing and size of dilutive capital raises against accumulated losses (equity fell from NZ$39.9m FY2022 to NZ$4.8m FY2025 as losses accumulated, then jumped to NZ$25.6m FY2026 on the Aug-2025 raise), not by retained-earnings compounding -- a -9.0%/+3.6% CAGR pair describes financing events, not business quality. The only meaningful growth anchor is the disclosed platform-subscription-revenue series (management's own segment disclosure, +33% FY26, corroborated by 1Q FY27 ERR +31% and guidance of 33-35% for FY27), which is what the base-case revenue path is built from at the segment level (subscription/transactional/hardware) rather than from a single blended historical CAGR.

base.narrative: Base case: the guided 33-35% FY27 subscription growth is achieved roughly at the low end and decelerates gradually as the ~5-6%-penetrated addressable market (US$1.1-1.4tn utility capex 2025-30, ~130m aging poles) is worked through; Platform Transactions stabilises after the FY26/1Q FY27 regulatory-driven decline rather than fully recovering, and Hardware & Other continues its gradual structural decline as subscription bundling replaces standalone device sales. Blended total-revenue growth (23% in Y1, decelerating to a 5% terminal rate) reflects subscription becoming ~85-90%+ of the mix over the horizon. Gross margin continues expanding toward the mid-80s as the mix shifts, and owner EBITDA margin (before SBC) crosses breakeven around Year 4-5 -- consistent with the operating leverage already visible from FY2024 (-9.8m Adj EBITDA, 60% GM) to FY2026 (-5.0m Adj EBITDA, 80% GM) -- reaching a mature ~27% margin by Year 10 as a debt-free, ~80%+-gross-margin vertical SaaS business at scale. The three new Customer Council-led 2H FY27 product launches and the PolePilot/IKE Vitruvius AI pricing lever are assumed to land on time but not to produce outsized upside beyond the guided range.

bull.narrative: Bull case: all three 2H FY27 Customer Council-led products (distribution grid management, next-gen make-ready engineering, the fibre/communications module) land on time and individually outperform prior launches as management believes possible; the PolePilot ~10% price increase sustains with no churn and IKE Vitruvius further lifts ARPU; cross-sell into the ~80%-unpenetrated existing customer base and continued new-logo wins push subscription growth to the 30-32% area (above the top of FY27 guidance) before decelerating more slowly than base as the grid-modernisation/BEAD super-cycle keeps demand elevated for longer. Faster fixed-cost absorption pushes owner EBITDA (before SBC) to breakeven by Year 3-4 and to a mature ~32% margin, slightly ahead of typical vertical-SaaS peers given IKE's asset-light US-utility relationships and 94% subscription gross margin.

bear.narrative: Bear case: the three new 2H FY27 products slip or underdeliver, 1Q FY27's below-guidance subscription growth (27-31% vs 33-35% guided) persists as the new normal rather than accelerating into 2H, and Platform Transactions revenue does not stabilise as US federal BEAD/regulatory funding volatility continues to weigh on the fibre/telecom segment. Bentley Systems and Osmose hold or extend share against IKE's smaller R&D and sales budget, and the ~10% PolePilot price rise cannot be repeated without triggering churn. Subscription growth decelerates quickly from 10% toward a 2.5% terminal rate; owner EBITDA (before SBC) never reaches breakeven within the 10-year horizon, still at -8% in Year 10, consistent with the going-concern risk flagged in the FY2026 annual report and the real possibility (not the base case, but not remote) of a further dilutive capital raise if this trajectory materialises.

scenario_narratives.base: Guided subscription growth achieved near the low end and decelerating as the addressable market is worked through; transactional revenue stabilises rather than recovers; owner EBITDA (pre-SBC) breaks even around Year 4-5 and matures at ~27%.
scenario_narratives.bull: All three 2H FY27 product launches succeed, AI-driven pricing sustains, cross-sell into the 80%-unpenetrated existing base accelerates growth above guidance; breakeven pulled forward to Year 3-4, mature margin ~32%.
scenario_narratives.bear: New products slip, transactional softness persists, competitive pressure from Bentley/Osmose intensifies; growth decelerates quickly to low single digits and the business never reaches EBITDA breakeven within the horizon, keeping renewed-dilution risk alive.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised above the 15% house default to 30% because IKE's FY27 growth guidance explicitly depends on three unlaunched, unproven products landing successfully in 2H FY27, 1Q FY27 growth (27-31%) was already tracking below the 33-35% guided range, and the company's own FY26 going-concern note states further losses are expected -- this is a real (if reduced) probability of another dilutive raise if the growth/margin trajectory disappoints, not a generic caution. Bull weight cut to 20% because it requires several largely independent things to go right simultaneously (all three new products succeed AND sustain pricing power AND transactional softness reverses AND competitive share holds), each individually plausible but jointly a minority outcome. Base at 50% reflects that the company has a genuine, well-evidenced operating inflection already underway (EBITDA loss narrowing every year, gross margin expanding every quarter, underlying monthly EBITDA breakeven already reached once) even if the precise growth rate undershoots guidance somewhat.

valuation_philosophy.summary: IKE is a small, debt-free, net-cash vertical-SaaS/hardware-analytics company mid-transition from a hardware/transactional model to a recurring subscription model, riding a well-documented multi-year North American grid-modernisation and broadband-buildout capex cycle from a genuinely low (~5-6%) market-penetration base. The FY2026 result shows real operating leverage (gross margin 60%->80%->82% FY24->FY26->1Q FY27; Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing from -NZ$9.8m to -NZ$5.0m) rather than just a growth story, and the company reached positive underlying monthly EBITDA for the first time in March 2026. However, on a fully SBC-expensed owner-FCF basis the business is still meaningfully cash-negative today, FY27 guidance leans on three unproven products landing in 2H FY27, and the long history of dilutive capital raises (share capital NZ$55m->NZ$134.5m, FY2019-FY2026, funding accumulated losses of NZ$47m->NZ$113.8m) is a real and only partially-retired risk. The valuation therefore rests heavily on the terminal years of a 10-year component build, since the current owner-FCF base is negative and the story is entirely about the path to, and durability of, a mature double-digit EBITDA margin.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY27 growth guidance (33-35%) depends on three unlaunched Customer Council-led products landing successfully in 2H FY27; 1Q FY27 growth (27-31%) was already tracking below range
Persistent softness in the lower-margin Platform Transactions segment, tied to volatile US federal broadband (BEAD) funding and regulatory administration outside IKE's control

Owner-FCF base is currently negative (-NZ$6.97m on the house/SBC-expensed basis) so most of the valuation sits in the terminal value -- a small change in the margin-maturity assumption or the horizon length moves the answer materially

Long history of dilutive equity raises to fund losses; the FY2026 going-concern note itself states further losses are expected in FY27, so renewed dilution risk is reduced but not eliminated if the growth/margin path disappoints
Small absolute scale (NZ$26.5m FY26 revenue) against much larger, better-capitalised competitors (Bentley Systems, Osmose) that can outspend on AI feature velocity and sales coverage
USD-generated revenue against NZD consolidated reporting introduces real translation noise to reported (though not necessarily constant-currency) growth and margins
